expectations.text: Declares the readers: support leads and backend engineers
expectations.evidence: "**Readers:** Support leads (what changes for support, and when); backend engineers (data volume and delivery constraints)".

expectations.text: States the problem with concrete evidence from the brief (212 requests in October, or the Lumen Logistics churn) before the detailed solution and its constraints
expectations.evidence: "## Problem" lists "Support handled 212 of these requests in October" and Lumen Logistics churn; it precedes "Constraints for engineering" (the Summary before it is a brief proposal statement).

expectations.text: States an objective or goal the solution is measured against
expectations.evidence: "## Goals" e.g. "Requests to support for emailed usage reports fall once customers can schedule their own."

expectations.text: Lists out of scope: PDF exports, custom column selection, and the Starter plan
expectations.evidence: "## Non-goals": PDF exports; custom column selection; exports for the Starter plan.

expectations.text: Gives each reader group the content it needs: what changes for support and when, and the volume and delivery constraints for engineers
expectations.evidence: "What changes for support" incl. "Release date: not set yet..."; "Constraints for engineering" gives Volume (2M rows a month) and Delivery (signed link, 7 days).

expectations.text: Explains that exports arrive as a signed link valid for 7 days and why: attachments fail for accounts with 2M+ rows
expectations.evidence: Summary: "a signed download link that stays valid for 7 days. The file itself is not attached, because large accounts produce more than 2M rows a month."

expectations.text: The proposal itself appears within the first few paragraphs, before supporting detail
expectations.evidence: "## Summary" is the first section and states the proposal.
